name: Employment Pass (EP Categories I, II, III)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a basic monthly salary (excluding allowances, bonuses, and benefits-in-kind) of at least RM 20,000, effective for applications from 1 June 2026 -- double the prior RM 10,000 threshold. Exempt from mandatory succession planning. Capped at a maximum 10 years' cumulative duration with the same employer.
requirements.fix_path: Negotiate a basic salary at or above RM 20,000/month with the sponsoring employer.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a job offer from a Malaysian-registered company that meets local-hiring obligations before submitting the application.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a job offer from a compliant Malaysian employer.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a basic monthly salary of RM 10,000-19,999, effective from 1 June 2026 (up from the prior RM 5,000-9,999 range). Requires a documented succession plan showing how a Malaysian employee will be trained to eventually take over the role. Capped at 10 years' cumulative duration with the same employer.
requirements.fix_path: Negotiate a basic salary within the RM 10,000-19,999 range and prepare a succession plan.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a basic monthly salary of RM 5,000-9,999, effective from 1 June 2026 (up from the prior RM 3,000-4,999 range). Requires a documented succession plan. Capped at 5 years' cumulative duration with the same employer -- half Category I/II's cap.
requirements.fix_path: Negotiate a basic salary within the RM 5,000-9,999 range and prepare a succession plan.

evidence_required.document: Employment contract meeting the applicable category's basic-salary floor (excluding allowances/bonuses)
Succession plan documenting local-hire development (Category II and III)
Medical examination (chest X-ray, blood tests) and local-hiring-obligation compliance from the employer

outcome.duration_length: up to 10 years cumulative (Categories I and II) or 5 years cumulative (Category III) with the same employer, a new hard cap effective 1 June 2026 replacing the prior indefinite-renewal system

sources.title: ShineWing TY Teoh -- Employment Pass Minimum Salary Malaysia 2026 Guide, citing the Expatriate Services Division (ESD), Immigration Department of Malaysia's official 15 January 2026 announcement of the revised thresholds
Link Compliance -- Malaysia's New Employment Pass Rules (w.e.f. 1 June 2026), independently corroborating the same category thresholds and the 10-year/5-year cumulative caps

notes: STATUS: DRAFT (no direct MOHA/Immigration Department fetch achieved for the exact 2026 thresholds in this research pass, despite strong cross-corroboration across independent sources). STRUCTURAL FINDING, and the largest single Employment Pass overhaul in a decade -- unchanged since December 2016 until this reform: effective 1 June 2026, Category I doubled from RM 10,000 to RM 20,000/month, Category II rose from RM 5,000-9,999 to RM 10,000-19,999, and Category III moved from RM 3,000-4,999 to RM 5,000-9,999 -- all calculated on basic salary only, explicitly excluding allowances, bonuses, and benefits-in-kind, a frequently-misunderstood distinction per multiple sources checked. Approved by Cabinet 17 October 2025, announced by the Ministry of Home Affairs 14-15 January 2026, with a roughly 6-month compliance runway before the 1 June 2026 effective date -- existing passes remain valid until their own expiry, but any renewal filed from 1 June 2026 onward must meet the new thresholds. A second, structurally separate change bundled into the same reform: Employment Passes now carry a hard maximum cumulative duration with the same employer for the first time -- 10 years for Categories I and II, 5 years for Category III -- replacing indefinite renewal; extensions beyond the cap require case-by-case justification on national-interest grounds. Category II and III applications now require a documented succession plan showing local-hire development, mandatory and enforceable (MOHA has stated failure to implement a plan is grounds for renewal refusal) -- Category I is explicitly exempt from this requirement. A separately-administered regime applies to companies incorporated in Labuan (a federal territory with its own offshore financial-services framework): the Labuan Work Permit retains a RM 10,000/month floor, unaffected by the June 2026 EP reform -- flagged as a genuine parallel system worth noting for anyone structuring employment through a Labuan entity. From 1 June 2026, Dependent Pass eligibility was also extended to Category III holders for the first time (previously only Categories I and II could sponsor dependents) -- captured on my_dependent_pass rather than here. citizenship_after_months (144) reflects the long pipeline via my_permanent_residence's professional/points track (5 years to PR eligibility) plus the general 10-of-12-years naturalisation requirement documented in my_naturalisation -- among the longest work-based citizenship pipelines in this dataset, reflecting Malaysia's generally restrictive approach to both permanent residence and citizenship for economic migrants.
